proofs.text: Sign `RULE-1` as `jane@acme.com` with signing configured, then count the signature at gate `signed` against that list and against `someone@else.com`, and at gate `strong` against the second list; verify the first counts, the second is refused with a reason naming the signer list, and the third counts

reasons: PROOF-25 missing_trigger: Nothing runs before the assertion, so the proof reads an artifact that exists whether or not the code is right.
rule_text: Under `signed` a signature counts only when the commit that added it is signed, its author is on the signer list and that author did not last touch the test; under `strong` a committed signature from anyone counts

tests.body:
def test_what_a_counting_signature_is_at_each_gate(self, proved):
        signing_key(proved.root)
        sign_module.main(['login', 'RULE-1', '--project-root', proved.root])
        found = proved.load()[('login', 'RULE-1')][0]

        counted, reason = purlin_signatures.counts(
            proved.root, found, ['jane@acme.com'], gate='signed')
        assert counted, reason

        counted, reason = purlin_signatures.counts(
            proved.root, found, ['someone@else.com'], gate='signed')
        assert not counted and 'signer is not on the list' in reason

        counted, reason = purlin_signatures.counts(
            proved.root, found, ['someone@else.com'], gate='strong')
        assert counted, (
            'under strong a signature from anyone settles what the machine '
            'could not: %s' % reason)
tests.name: test_what_a_counting_signature_is_at_each_gate
